第 28 章 The Five Whys of Organizational Design组织设计的五个为什么

Kellan Elliott McCrea / 凯兰·埃利奥特·麦克雷

— 第 85 页 —

Recently, I wrote about sizing engineering organizations and how you can think about it as an exercise in managing concurrency. In understanding organization size, I talk about the mental exercise of thinking about how the number of concurrent work streams you're taking on as a team applies upward pressure on the needs of your organization (e.g., you need more managers, who need more directors, who need a more senior CTO, etc.) The inverse exercise is also useful.

最近，我写了关于工程组织规模的文章，以及如何把它看作管理并发的练习。在理解组织规模时，我谈到了一个思维练习：思考你作为团队同时承担的工作流数量如何对组织的需求施加向上压力（例如你需要更多经理，他们需要更多总监，他们需要更高级的 CTO 等）。反过来做这个练习也很有用。

As is so often the case with conversations about organizational design, the problem statement usually starts like this: "We need a new engineering leader. Should we hire a new vice president of engineering and move all our managers there (except, of course, for that one team)? Should we hire a CTO to own architectural conversations but maybe not have anyone report to them? Maybe this half of our team could report to the CPO?"

就像组织设计对话中经常出现的那样，问题陈述通常这样开头：「我们需要一个新的工程领导。我们应该招一个新的工程 VP 然后把所有经理都归他管吗（当然除了那个团队）？我们应该招一个 CTO 来负责架构讨论但可能没人向他汇报吗？也许我们这一半团队可以向 CPO 汇报？」

I spend a lot of time trying to convince teams that this is the wrong way to think about organizational design. You can't solve questions of organizational design by shuffling responsibilities around the board like so many chips on the roulette table (or memorably, once, like so many stacks of Starburst candy on the floor of the CEO's office). And you can't solve your team's problems by slicing more thinly the responsibilities at the top, no matter how often someone tells you the hoary distinction that the vice president of engineering is there to manage people and the CTO is there to make technical decisions (a distinction that is not only bad and wrong, but will eventually leave your company a pile of burning rubble). These are the wrong questions. So, what are the correct questions?

我花很多时间试图说服团队这是思考组织设计的错误方式。你不能通过像轮盘赌桌上的筹码一样把责任在棋盘上 shuffling 来解决组织设计问题（或者有一次令人难忘的像 CEO 办公室地板上一堆 Starburst 糖一样）。你也不能通过把顶层责任切得更细来解决团队问题，不管多少次有人告诉你那个老掉牙的区分：工程 VP 是管人、CTO 是做技术决策（这个区分不仅糟糕而且错误，最终会让你的公司变成一堆燃烧的瓦砾）。这些都是错误的问题。那么，正确的问题是什么？

Get Curious保持好奇

When faced with these problems, I find it useful to walk the stack down to the front line of work to understand what the pressures on this complex system are. Call it the "Five (possibly rhetorical) Whys of Organizational Design."

面对这些问题时，我发现沿着栈一路走到工作前线很有用，来理解这个复杂系统上的压力是什么。叫它「组织设计的五个（可能是反问的）为什么」吧。

— 第 86 页 —

Q1: Why can't your CTO/vice president of engineering/head of engineering create the context where these problems are getting solved? A: Well, they're just spread really thin.

Q1：为什么你的 CTO/工程 VP/工程负责人不能创造让这些问题被解决的上下文？ A：他们实在分身乏术。

Q2: So why aren't your directors helping take the load off? A: Well, they're spread really thin as well (or we don't have them).

Q2：那为什么你的总监不帮忙分担？ A：他们也分身乏术（或者我们没有总监）。

Q3: So why aren't your engineering managers taking load off the directors? A: They're spread really thin as well; we just promoted one of them from being a senior engineer, etc.

Q3：那为什么你的工程经理不帮总监分担？ A：他们也分身乏术；我们刚把其中一个从高级工程师提上来等等。

Q4: So why aren't your tech leads taking load off your managers? A: They're spread really thin (or we don't have them).

Q4：那为什么你的技术负责人不帮经理分担？ A：他们分身乏术（或者我们没有技术负责人）。

Q5: So why aren't your senior engineers taking load off your tech leads?

Q5：那为什么你的高级工程师不帮技术负责人分担？

And by now we often get to the interesting actionable answers.

到这里我们通常就能得到有趣的、可行动的答案了。

Some Common Discoveries Along the Way一路上的一些常见发现

Having walked the hierarchy of organizational dysfunction, we can now start prescribing slightly more tailored responses than the leadership equivalent of "turn it off, and turn it back on again." Thankfully, many organizations face similar challenges, and we can catalog a few of the most common.

走过了组织功能失调的层级之后，我们现在可以开始开比领导层版的「关掉再开」更有针对性的药方了。谢天谢地，很多组织面临类似的挑战，我们可以列出几个最常见的。

  • Your head of engineering doesn't have anyone to whom they can delegate organizational work ⇒ you need directors.你的工程负责人没有人可以把组织工作授权出去 ⇒ 你需要总监。
  • Your directors are spending all their time managing and can't contribute to organizational capacity ⇒ you need managers.你的总监把所有时间花在管理上、不能为组织产能做贡献 ⇒ 你需要经理。
  • Your managers are spending all their time dealing with the fact that their team is composed of humans ⇒ they either need fewer direct reports or to be managing people in a less drama-inducing work place.你的经理把所有时间花在处理团队由人组成这个事实上 ⇒ 他们要么需要更少的直接下属，要么需要在一个不那么狗血的工作场所管人。
  • Your managers are spending all their time tech leading ⇒ you need tech leads.你的经理把所有时间花在当技术负责人上 ⇒ 你需要技术负责人。
  • Your managers are spending too much time reviewing PRs ⇒ stop being a control freak and trust your team. You're hiring smart people to make good decisions. If you can't trust them, that's a leadership failure.你的经理花太多时间评审 PR ⇒ 别做控制狂了，信任你的团队。你招聪明人来做好的决策。如果你不能信任他们，那是领导力的失败。
  • Your managers are spending too much time coding ⇒ you need more engineers or you need to do less.你的经理花太多时间写代码 ⇒ 你需要更多工程师或者你需要少做点。
— 第 87 页 —
  • You don't have tech leads because every team is super small, maybe one engineer per team ⇒ you're doing too many things. Also, you like failing.你没有技术负责人因为每个团队都超级小，可能每队一个工程师 ⇒ 你在做太多事情。而且，你喜欢失败。
  • Your tech leads spend all their time reviewing PRs ⇒ seriously, stop it.你的技术负责人把所有时间花在评审 PR 上 ⇒ 说真的，别这样了。
  • Your tech leads and/or senior engineers spend all their time coding ⇒ your definition of senior doesn't include leadership. You need to fix that. Likely as far back as your hiring process.你的技术负责人和/或高级工程师把所有时间花在写代码上 ⇒ 你对高级的定义不包含领导力。你需要修正它。很可能要追溯到你的招聘流程。
  • Your senior engineers are busy working on less-important things ⇒ it's possible communication has broken down. Or maybe prioritization isn't as clear as you thought it was?你的高级工程师忙于做不太重要的事情 ⇒ 可能沟通已经崩溃了。或者优先级没有你想的那么清晰？
  • Your senior engineers are spending all their time firefighting ⇒ likely you've created insufficient slack in the system to allow for training and tool building.你的高级工程师把所有时间花在火上 ⇒ 可能你在系统里创造的余量不足，无法用于培训和工具建设。
  • Your senior engineers don't have anyone to mentor/train, they're discouraged by the constant firefighting, they've become cynical about your lack of ability to plan, and they'd like to wander off and just build something shiny to give their brain a rest ⇒ did you do that thing where you "hire only seniors," because that's what it sounds like. Alternatively, did you do that thing where you spent a lot of energy selling your "hard technical problems" during your interview loop, but having those problems was a bit…aspirational?你的高级工程师没有人可以辅导/培训，他们被持续救火打击了积极性，对你缺乏计划能力变得愤世嫉俗，他们想走开去做一些闪亮的东西让大脑休息一下 ⇒ 你是不是做了那个「只招高级」的事情？因为听起来就是那样。或者，你是不是做了那个在面试环节花很多精力推销你「困难的技术问题」、但拥有那些问题有点…… aspirational 的事情？
  • Your CTO/vice president of engineering/head of engineering doesn't actually want to think about any of these problems. ⇒ are you sure? Have you asked them? If so, you're right, you need a new head of engineering.你的 CTO/工程 VP/工程负责人其实不想思考这些问题。⇒ 你确定吗？你问过他们了吗？如果问过了，那你是对的，你需要一个新的工程负责人。
